locations.name: Rowanstead
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

locations.name: Vesperhold
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

locations.name: Fernbridge
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

locations.name: The Hushwood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

locations.name: The Broken Sanctuary
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

locations.name: The Crownspine
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

locations.name: The Glasswater Fen
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

locations.name: Saltbell Harbor
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

locations.name: The Glass Observatory
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

locations.name: The Wandering Hearth
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

locations.name: The Brassward Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

locations.name: The Bastion of Bells
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

locations.name: The Ancestor’s Rest
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Vesperhold, necromancy is regulated; in Rowanstead, it is forbidden; in Fernbridge, it is permitted. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Families honor willing ancestors with named memorials; a person’s consent matters beyond death.

festival.name: The First Moon Fair
festival.tradition: Apprentices display their work beside the oldest local craft masters.

event.title: The arms that first held you
event.body: Your guardians decide what kind of shelter to make around this new life. The rain leaves the courtyard smelling of rosemary. Your household has little money, but people can offer time and teaching. A winter seed sprouted beside your cradle, its roots pointing toward the burial ground. Your family will remember the sign; its meaning must be discovered through childhood.

hero.name: Aster
hero.ambition: Protect the place I call home

world.name: The Willowlands

locations.name: Wrenfield
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

locations.name: Goldmere
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

locations.name: Cresswater
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Public necromantic practice is prohibited. Authorities require a witness or evidence before opening an investigation.

locations.name: The Greywood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

locations.name: The Ashen Cloister
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

locations.name: The Crownspine
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

locations.name: The Reedwaste
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

locations.name: Saltbell Harbor
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

locations.name: The Starwatch Tower
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

locations.name: The Wandering Hearth
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

locations.name: The Brassward Crossing
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

locations.name: The Bastion of Bells
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

locations.name: The Ancestor’s Rest
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Goldmere, necromancy is permitted; in Wrenfield, it is forbidden; in Cresswater, it is forbidden. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Lanterns are left on doorsteps for travelers, and a promise spoken at a hearth is expected to be kept.

festival.name: The Returning Lanterns
festival.tradition: Families share a public meal and leave a place for absent friends.

rumors: The academy in Goldmere is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Greywood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Dame Mara Alder
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Scholar Tamsin
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: Merrin Shade
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.

companions.name: Mira
companions.goal: Earn a place in the Lantern Order without abandoning old friends.
memories: At seven, you helped turn an accusation into cooperation.
We began traveling together after growing up as friends.

companions.name: Orrin
companions.goal: Find a remedy for the fever and keep his family safe.
memories: You invited me to travel as a healer, without asking me to forget my family.

companions.name: Kest
companions.goal: Make the western road safe enough to visit a missing sibling.
values: Do not prey on desperate families
memories: You invited me onto the road while respecting my search for my sibling.

legal.description: No local charges or known evidence.

world.name: The Willowlands

locations.name: Hearthmere
locations.description: A small settlement of hearth fires, kitchen gardens, and familiar faces. Ashfall fever has reached its households; the old shrine is still a place to seek help. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

locations.name: Brindlehall
locations.description: The region’s busy city gathers an academy, a guild market, and a sworn order behind its stone walls. Fever wards are filling, and scholars disagree over the cause. Willing ancestral rites and the study of the dead are permitted; coercion and grave theft remain crimes.

locations.name: Brookhollow
locations.description: A riverside village where millers, ferrymen, and herbalists trade news. Families are sheltering travelers fleeing Ashfall fever. Ancestral rites require a witness or academy license; raising bodies and binding unwilling souls are prohibited.

locations.name: The Copperwood
locations.description: Old trails connect both villages beneath a canopy of moss and copper leaves. Healing herbs grow here, alongside hungry beasts and abandoned camps. The nearest settlement’s law governs witnessed acts.

locations.name: The Broken Sanctuary
locations.description: An abandoned sanctuary beyond the forest holds sealed research and the memories of its former keepers. Licensed expeditions may study its ancestral records; disturbing remains without consent invites scrutiny.

locations.name: The Stormward Peaks
locations.description: Wind-carved passes and abandoned mines cross the northern mountains. Guides keep a refuge beneath the high stones.

locations.name: The Mourning Mire
locations.description: Lanterns mark a boardwalk through deep reed beds. Apothecaries gather rare remedies beside drowned foundations.

locations.name: Saltbell Harbor
locations.description: A harbor of salt-white sails, fisher families, and traders from distant provinces. New arrivals bring both opportunity and rumor.

locations.name: The Glass Observatory
locations.description: A lonely observatory studies the stars and preserves knowledge beyond the city academy’s reach. Its keepers welcome careful learners.

locations.name: The Copper Caravan
locations.description: Travelers, scouts, and craftspeople share a guarded camp. A meal and an honest story can earn a place by the communal fire.

locations.name: The Covenant Arch
locations.description: An ancient gateway controls the road into the uplands. Watchers record travelers, while weathered carvings hint at older promises.

locations.name: The Thornward Keep
locations.description: A fortified settlement overlooks the eastern roads. Orders and guilds offer an alternative to the city’s institutions.

locations.name: The Grove of Mercy
locations.description: A protected sanctuary shelters displaced families and teachers. Its doors remain open when other institutions fall silent.

world.laws: Local councils set their own rules. In Brindlehall, necromancy is permitted; in Hearthmere, it is permitted; in Brookhollow, it is regulated. Authorities act on witnesses, reports, and discovered evidence. Willing ancestral contact, grave theft, and unwilling soul binding are treated as different acts.
world.culture: Wild groves are protected as common ground, and moon watchers teach respect for changing seasons.

festival.name: The Hearthlight Gathering
festival.tradition: Neighbors exchange handmade gifts and tell stories of the year.

rumors: The academy in Brindlehall is seeking careful field observers, not only wealthy students.
A moonwise ranger near The Copperwood can teach a refuge ritual without demanding allegiance.
Licensed ancestral research is attracting healers from distant villages.

mentors.name: Ser Elian Vale
mentors.description: A sworn protector offers training and an initiation founded on a visible oath of mercy and protection.

mentors.name: Archivist Iona
mentors.description: A physician teaches consensual ancestral rites and sponsors students studying the ruined archive.

mentors.name: Vey the Quiet
mentors.description: A discreet contact offers a test of stealth and judgment, with the terms disclosed before accepting.
